text:
**Short answer:** The file holds no earlier Toil & Trouble cases to draw from. The only Toil & Trouble matter in the client store is *Okafor v. Toil & Trouble Home Products*, No. D-2026-1184. If B-2 is a new or related claim, the facts below from Okafor are the ones most likely to recur. I have not used anything from the firm's other clients' matters (Telltale, Joad). That material is confidential to those clients and shouldn't inform this one.

**Retail and return history**
- Okafor bought the unit from Marlowe Home & Hardware on October 11, 2024 for $119.99. A retail employee told the client's investigator that the box was returned once and resold as new. This is unverified, but it bears on whether any buyer got a new unit.
- Customer care logged one contact in July 2025 from a household at the Okafor address about a replacement gasket. A gasket was sent, but the shipment records have not yet been pulled. If another claimant has a similar history, expect the same alteration and wrong-part argument.
- Ask Marlowe to preserve its sales records, and find out whether any unit was bought new or through another channel.

**Engineering and quality identifiers**
- Product: PressureMate TT-6200, a six-quart electric pressure cooker with a rotating bayonet lid, a spring-loaded float valve and a lockout pin. Operating pressure is about 10 psi.
- Lot: the Q3-2024 lot has no field lid complaints. Line inspection records for the week of manufacture have been agreed for production.
- Complaints: three "lid hard to open" complaints on other 2024 lots. Plaintiff will frame them as notice. Complaints are tracked in the Ravenscar ticketing system.
- Design change: ECN-6200-14 added a retention clip to the lockout pin on later production. It is dated after Okafor's purchase but before her injury, so the subsequent-remedial-measure rule probably won't exclude it. How to treat it should be settled before the design file goes out on June 5, 2026.
- Sibling model: the TT-5500 uses the same lockout pin but a different locking ring and lid seat. Its complaints are producible only where the report describes the pin as the failing element (the May 1 compromise).
- Safety listing: an independent laboratory listing, with supporting test reports agreed for production.

**People and theories**
- Technical contact: Rennick Odell, product safety lead. He is the one fact deposition allowed before mediation on our proposal.
- Plaintiff's experts: Dr. Gareth Pellam, who will say starch or bean foam makes the pin stick, and Dr. Yvette Hargrove, a human-factors witness on the warnings.
- Our consulting engineer: Dr. Oswin Takahashi.

**Handling cautions**
- Don't volunteer complaint history or other incidents until a request is served and scope is discussed.
- Report any other TT-6200 or related-model claim to Mr. Oyelaran promptly, copying Delphine Moorcroft.
- Tell Mr. Oyelaran at once if any claim could lead to a product pull, because of the retailer advance-warning promise.

If you meant other Toil & Trouble matters outside this file, send me the details. I can't confirm they exist from what I have.
